deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The top of the page is a French draft letter, Pisa 1863, to M. Valéry in Livorno. It concerns a crate (K-3-1, 'caisse vieux livres et effets', 215 fr) shipped by M. Romagni & Cie of Marseille on the packet boat 'Prince Napoléon'. It matches the German letter to the Consul on the previous page. Below it are two blocks of mathematics. Both concern theta functions with half-period characteristics on a hyperelliptic Riemann surface.

(A) ALTERNATING BILINEAR FORM.
Let a_i, a_i' (i = 1..2p+2) be the coefficients (0/1 mod 2) of the branch points in two half-periods. Riemann writes
F(a,a') = (a2'-a1') a1 + (a4'-a3')(a3-a2+a1) + (a6'-a5')(a5-a4+a3-a2+a1) + ...
In modern terms, F(a,a') = sum_k (a'_{2k} - a'_{2k-1}) S_{2k-1}(a), with S_m(a) = a_m - a_{m-1} + ... ± a_1. This is the pairing for a canonical homology basis in which the cycles encircle consecutive branch points on a line.

He then regroups the result by the unprimed variables. The final line
a1(a2'-a3'+a4'-...) + a2(-a1'+a3'-a4'+...) + a3(a1'-a2'+a4'-...) + ...
is exactly the coefficient-wise expansion of G = F(a,a') - F(a',a). I verified this; the reading as the antisymmetrisation is mine. In the a1 line the crossed-out first entry is precisely the term -a1' that cancels between F(a,a') and F(a',a).

Closed form (mine): G = sum_{i<j} (-1)^{i+j+1} (a_i a_j' - a_j a_i'). Modulo 2 this is sum_{i≠j} a_i a_j' = |A||A'| - |A∩A'|. That is the Weil/symplectic pairing of two half-periods written as sums of branch points. Riemann needs it to decide which characteristics are even or odd and which systems are syzygetic or azygetic.

(B) COUNTING.
- 9·10/(1·2) = 45 = C(10,2) and 7·8·9·10/(1·2·3·4) = 210 = C(10,4). With 10 = 2p+2 for p = 4, these count subsets of branch points, i.e. half-periods of a given type.
- The rows '9 5 1 / 7 3' look like a parity sorting of subset sizes.

(C) GENERALISED JACOBI DERIVATIVE FORMULA, p = 5.
There are 2p+2 = 12 branch points, split as a1..a5 and b1..b7 (p+2 = 7 b's; hence the lists 'b5 b6 b7', '1234', 'b_j + Σb'). Riemann writes
Σ± ϑ'_1(Σ_1 a) ϑ'_2(Σ_2 a) ... ϑ'_5(Σ_5 a) = Π_{j=1}^{7} ϑ(b_j + Σa).
Σ± denotes a determinant. Σ_i a is most plausibly the sum of the a's other than a_i (p-1 = 4 points). In Mumford's later normalisation such a sum gives an odd nonsingular characteristic, while b_j + Σa (p+1 = 6 points) gives an even nonsingular one.
Modern form: det[∂ϑ[η_{A∖a_i}](0)/∂z_k] = c · Π_{b∉A} ϑ[η_{A∪b}](0), with |A| = p. For p = 1 this is Jacobi's ϑ1' = π ϑ2 ϑ3 ϑ4 (3 = p+2 factors). For p = 2 it is Rosenhain's formula (4 factors).
The vertical-line sketch with the a's and b's marked along it is the arrangement of branch points and cycles used in (A).

(D) p = 4, A MIXED DETERMINANT (partly illegible).
Σ± ϑ'(Σc) ϑ'(Σ_2 a) ϑ'(Σ_3 a) ϑ'(Σ_4 a) = Π_b ϑ(a1+b1+Σc) Π_c ϑ(c+Σa) + Π_c ϑ(a1+c+Σb) Π_b ϑ(b).
Here one odd characteristic is taken from a different set, so the Jacobian is no longer of the 'fundamental' type. Riemann tries to express it as a sum of two products of even theta constants. This is an attempt beyond the product case, and it cannot be checked from the image (indices partly illegible).

A further line, Σ± ϑ'(a1+Σb) = Π ϑ(b+Σc) ϑb' ... Π(b+Σa) ϑ(b+Σa), is a fragmentary intermediate version of (C)/(D).
errors: The juxtaposed lines 'a1(a2'-a3'+a4'...)' and '= a1'(a2-a3+a4...)' are not an identity. They are two halves of the antisymmetrised form written one under the other; the '=' should not be read as an equation.

In the first expansion attempt, 'a2(-a1'+a' ...' is left incomplete. The final line is correct for the antisymmetrised form G = F(a,a') - F(a',a), not for F itself. In F alone the coefficient of a1 would be -a1'+a2'-a3'+..., which is the version Riemann crossed out.

In the p=5 formula the upper index of the product is written ambiguously ('Π', apparently the number p+2 = 7). No constant (power of π, sign, or algebraic modulus factor) is written. The formula is valid only up to such a constant.

The p=4 two-term formula cannot be verified as read. The index sets (Σc, Σb, a1+b1+Σc) are only partially legible. Its form (a sum of two products) is plausible for non-fundamental triples/quadruples, but its correctness is unconfirmed.

results.what: Antisymmetric bilinear form G = Σ_{i<j} (-1)^{i+j+1}(a_i a_j' - a_j a_i') for half-periods written as sums of branch points (mod 2: |A||A'| - |A∩A'|)
results.modern_name: Weil pairing / symplectic intersection form on 2-torsion of a hyperelliptic Jacobian, in terms of branch-point sets
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's theory of characteristics (published via Weber 1876, Thomae 1870); in the set-theoretic form Mumford, Tata Lectures II (1984)

results.what: Binomial counts C(10,2) = 45 and C(10,4) = 210 for subsets of the 2p+2 = 10 branch points (p = 4)
results.modern_name: Counting half-periods / theta characteristics via branch-point subsets

results.what: Determinant of gradients of p odd theta functions ϑ[Σ_{a≠a_i}a] equals a product of p+2 even theta constants ϑ[b_j+Σa] (written for p = 5)
results.modern_name: Hyperelliptic generalisation of Jacobi's derivative formula (Rosenhain–Thomae–Frobenius formula)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (p=1), Rosenhain 1851 (p=2), general hyperelliptic case Thomae (c.1870) / Frobenius 1885; modern treatment Igusa 1980, Fay

results.what: Attempt (p = 4) to express a Jacobian determinant of a non-fundamental system of odd characteristics as a sum of two products of even theta constants
results.modern_name: Jacobian nullwerte for non-fundamental systems (sums of products of theta constants)

deep.surprise_reason: The bilinear-form computation is routine for Riemann, whose characteristic theory is well known through Weber and Thomae. However, an explicit general-p (written for p=5) hyperelliptic Jacobi derivative formula, with the correct p+2 even factors ϑ(b_j+Σa) and odd characteristics Σ_{a≠a_i}a, dated 1863 in Riemann's own hand, predates Thomae's and Frobenius's published treatments. It is a notable unpublished detail, though Thomae (Riemann's student) plausibly drew on Riemann's lectures, so it is not wholly unexpected. The p=4 attempt at a non-product Jacobian is more unusual but too fragmentary to rate higher.

checkable.asserts: Coefficients are b2-b3+b4-b5+b6, -b1+b3-b4+b5-b6, b1-b2+b4-b5+b6, matching Riemann's final line a1(a2'-a3'+a4'..)+a2(-a1'+a3'-a4'..)+a3(a1'-a2'+a4'..).

checkable.sympy: expand(F(A,B)-F(B,A) - sum((-1)**(i+j+1)*(A[i]*B[j]-A[j]*B[i]) for i in range(6) for j in range(i+1,6))) == 0
checkable.asserts: Closed form G = Σ_{i<j} (-1)^{i+j+1}(a_i a_j' - a_j a_i') for six branch-point coefficients (holds only for the even truncation n = 6 used here).
For p=4 the branch-point subsets account for all 136 even and 120 odd theta characteristics.
For p=5, odd characteristics are sums of p-1=4 (or 0) of the 12 branch points (496 in total), consistent with ϑ'(Σ_i a) being odd.
p=1 case of the formula (Jacobi derivative formula, z-normalisation): result is 0, with p+2=3 even factors.

transcription_corrections: 'Romagni[?]' is better read 'Romagnè' or 'Romagni' (uncertain), followed by 'Cie de Marseille'.
In '= a1'(a2 - a3 + a4 ...)' the a3 carries an overwritten superscript (looks like a 5); the line is not a genuine equation.
In 'a1([-1-]+a2'-a3'+a4'...)' the struck item is most likely a1' (the cancelling -a1' term), not the digit 1. In the a2 term a struck 'a2'' stands before '+a3''.
'Σ ± ϑ'_1Σa ϑ'_2Σ_2a ... ϑ'_5Σ_5a = Π ϑ(b1+Σa) ... ϑ(b_7+Σa)': the subscript on the last factor appears to be 7 (=p+2), not 'Π'.
'b_4+Σ2[?]' at right is probably 'b_4+Σa'; the column 'a1+Σb, a2+Σb, a3+Σb, a4' should read a4+Σb.
'b1 b2 b3 + b5' is probably a list of index sets (b1 b2 b3 ... b5), not a sum.
